activities.title: Dynamic Warm Up
activities.summary: Range of motion and warm up activities to prepare the body for training.
activities.description:
- Jog
- Quads, Hamstrings
- Open/Close Gates
- Lunge + Twist
- Backward Runs
- Figure 4's
- Sideways Runs
- Header + Sprint
- Strides
activities.field_setup: 2-4 lines of players
activities.coaching_points:
- Full range of motion on each movement
- Control and targeted stretch over speed and burst
activities.flexibility_notes:
- Players can add individual stretches as needed
- Volleys or rondos can be appended to extend to 20 minutes

activities.title: Volleys
activities.summary: Partner volley work covering instep, laces, chest, thigh, and header technique.
activities.description:
- Pair up with a partner
- Instep volley (5-10 reps each)
- Laces volley (5-10 reps each)
- Chest volley (5-10 reps each)
- Thigh volley (5-10 reps each)
- Header (5-10 reps each)
- Adjust distance as quality improves
activities.field_setup: Pairs spread across field, ~10 yards apart
activities.coaching_points:
- Firm, flat surface on contact
- Eye on the ball through contact
- Body shape: bent knees, stable base
- Aim for chest height to partner
activities.flexibility_notes:
- Can extend to include hip volleys and bring-it-down progressions
- Add triangle headers as a group variation

activities.title: Triangle Headers
activities.summary: Three-player heading circuit to build aerial comfort and directional accuracy.
activities.description:
- 3 players form a triangle, ~5-8 yards apart
- Player 1 throws to Player 2
- Player 2 heads to Player 3
- Player 3 catches and throws to Player 1
- Continue cycling
- Progress: all players head rather than catching
activities.field_setup: Groups of 3, triangle ~5-8 yards per side
activities.coaching_points:
- Eyes open, attack the ball
- Strike with the forehead, not the top of the head
- Heading technique: up and out
- Neck firm on contact
activities.flexibility_notes: - Increase triangle size for longer aerial work

activities.title: Brazilians
activities.summary: Paired volley circuit covering multiple surfaces to build first-touch quality from the air.
activities.description:
- Pair up with a partner
- Instep volley
- Laces volley
- Chest volley
- Thigh volley
- Bring it down (trap after volley)
- 5-10 reps each surface
activities.field_setup: Pairs spread across field, ~8-12 yards apart
activities.coaching_points:
- Lead with the correct surface for each variation
- Consistent pace to partner
- Focus on first touch quality, not just volume
activities.flexibility_notes: - Can be organized into groups by bib color for quick partner assignment

activities.title: Long Ball - Ground Passing
activities.summary: Progressive ground passing over increasing distances to develop accuracy and weight of pass.
activities.description:
- Groups of 2-3, starting ~15 yards apart
- Pass on the ground, switch to non-dominant foot halfway through
- 3-4 minutes at 15 yards, then progress to 20-25 yards
- Focus on clean technique: plant foot, locked ankle, follow through
activities.field_setup: Pairs on open grass, 15-25 yards apart
activities.coaching_points:
- Plant foot beside the ball
- Locked ankle, clean contact through center of ball
- Follow through toward target
- Use non-dominant foot for half of reps
activities.flexibility_notes: - Start at 10 yards for beginners, extend to 30+ for advanced players

activities.title: Long Ball - Air Passing
activities.summary: Chipped and lofted passes over distance to develop aerial distribution accuracy.
activities.description:
- Groups of 2-3, ~25 yards apart
- Send ball in the air to partner
- Partner controls and passes back
- Switch to non-dominant foot halfway through
- Focus on giving the ball air and landing accuracy
activities.field_setup: Pairs on open grass, 20-30 yards apart
activities.coaching_points:
- Lean back slightly to get under the ball
- Strike with instep at an angle for lift
- Target: ball should arrive comfortably at chest height
- Accuracy over power
activities.flexibility_notes: - Can pair with Chip and Juggle: chip to partner, partner juggles before passing back

activities.title: Chip and Juggle
activities.summary: Partner drill combining aerial delivery with juggle-to-control to build first-touch quality under aerial balls.
activities.description:
- Pairs ~20 yards apart
- Player chips ball to partner
- Partner juggles 2 times, then traps
- Progression: increase to 3 juggles
- Score a point for successfully completing the juggle target
activities.field_setup: Pairs, ~15-25 yards apart
activities.coaching_points:
- Soft, accurate chip: ball should arrive at a manageable height
- Eyes up early to track incoming ball
- Stay on toes, ready to adjust position
- Controlled juggle: deliberate contact, not reactive
activities.flexibility_notes:
- Start with 2-juggle requirement, increase as quality improves
- Can integrate into a larger fundamentals circuit with GK Hands Training

activities.title: GK Hands Training
activities.summary: Goalkeeper-specific handling and distribution drill to develop catch technique and throwing accuracy.
activities.description:
- Catches:
  - W grip for high balls: thumbs close together behind the ball
  - M grip for low balls: little fingers close together
  - Bring ball to the body to secure
- Overhand throws: straight arm, control release angle
- Underhand throws: full roll (no bounce), protected gathering
- Quick hands: rapid catch-and-release sequences
- Partner serves balls from ~8-12 yards to various heights and sides
activities.field_setup: GK with server, open space or in front of goal
activities.coaching_points:
- W grip: thumbs close behind ball for high shots
- M grip: pinkies close for low shots
- Bring the ball to the body to secure
- Follow through toward target on throws
activities.flexibility_notes: - Run simultaneously with field player technical work to maximize time efficiency

activities.title: Passing Lines - Short Short Long
activities.summary: Combination passing pattern with two short passes followed by a longer driven ball, developing pass rhythm and weight.
activities.description:
- 4-6 players per line
- Player passes short to teammate, runs to support
- Teammate passes short to next player
- Third player plays a longer driven ball down the line
- Pattern repeats
- Focus on pace of pass and timing of support runs
activities.field_setup: 2 parallel lines, ~30-40 yards total length
activities.coaching_points:
- Play ball that teammate can handle: don't overhit into space
- Adjust your run to accommodate teammate receiving ball
- Angle run to allow proper body shape and spacing
- Appropriate pace and control on each pass
activities.flexibility_notes:
- Can add a passive defender on the long ball for pressure
- Extend to include a shot at the end of the sequence

activities.title: Triangular Passing Pattern
activities.summary: Passing in small triangles to develop body shape, first touch, and pass timing.
activities.description:
- 4 players per triangle grid (8-yard sides)
- Ball starts with the corner that has two players
- Play ball to teammate, follow your pass to end of opposite line
- Receive ball across the body, play to next teammate
- Continue cycling
activities.field_setup: 4 triangle grids, 8-yard sides, 4 players per grid
activities.coaching_points:
- Adjust body position to create a clear option for your teammate
- Set up to receive on the turn with minimal extra touches
- Play the ball to the correct foot of your teammate
- Where are you passing: inside or outside foot?
activities.flexibility_notes:
- Increase grid size for longer combinations
- Can add a defender to increase pressure

activities.title: Passing Progression
activities.summary: Small group passing at progressively increasing distances to develop accuracy and weight of pass.
activities.description:
- Groups of 5
- Start ~10 yards apart, then increase to 15, 20, 25 yards
- As distance increases, introduce low driven passes
- Pass the ball, run to the end of the opposite line
- Receiver controls and plays back
activities.field_setup: Two lines, distance increases each round
activities.coaching_points:
- Clean control before passing
- Weight of pass should match the distance
- Run to end of line immediately after passing
- Low ping pass for longer distances: drive through center, keep it low
activities.flexibility_notes: - Stay at one distance longer if the group needs more reps

activities.title: Layoff Play Through Rondo Rotation
activities.summary: Hexagonal passing rotation with layoffs and diagonal passes to develop quick combination play and movement off the ball.
activities.description:
- Setup: hexagon with offset corners
- 4 players per hex
- Player passes to adjacent player, moves to next spot
- Receiving player lays off diagonally to next player
- Pattern continues around the hex
- Cycle directions regularly
activities.field_setup: Hexagon grid with offset corners, ~8-12 yards per side
activities.coaching_points:
- Quick layoff: don't hold the ball
- Anticipate the movement so the next pass is ready
- Good first touch in the direction of play
- Keep moving after passing
activities.flexibility_notes: - Allow two-touch for beginners

activities.title: Skill Moves Circuit
activities.summary: Guided circuit of 1v1 skill moves to develop close control and the ability to beat defenders.
activities.description:
- Step Overs: standard, rollover variation
- Cruyff Turn: cut behind standing leg to change direction
- Cruyff Escape: variation to evade a pressing defender
- Additional escape moves as introduced by coach
- Practice each move slowly first, then at game speed
- Pair up and apply moves on a passive then active defender
activities.field_setup: Open space, cone markers for 1v1 channels if needed
activities.coaching_points:
- Slow and deliberate before speeding up
- Body balance before executing the move
- Change of pace after the move is as important as the move itself
activities.flexibility_notes:
- Adjust list of moves to suit team's current repertoire
- Can dedicate the full time to a single move if needed

activities.title: Rondos
activities.summary: Possession game in a tight space with one or two defenders to develop quick passing, body shape, and decision making under pressure.
activities.description:
- 4-6 players on the outside, 1-2 defenders inside
- Outside players maintain possession
- Defender wins ball or forces out-of-bounds: rotate in
- Rotate defenders every 3-4 passes if ball is not won
- Variations: small (4v1), medium (5v1), large (5v2)
activities.field_setup: Circle or square, ~8-10 yards diameter for small, ~12-15 for larger
activities.coaching_points:
- Move to create openings before receiving
- Adapt body shape and plan passes in advance
- Move the ball quickly and accurately
- Play to the open foot of your teammate
activities.flexibility_notes:
- Add an end-zone target to give possession directional intent
- Add a third defender to increase difficulty

activities.title: Across the River - Wide Channels
activities.summary: Directional possession game with wide channel players to practice playing out of pressure, switching play, and maintaining shape.
activities.description:
- Outer grid: ~30x50, inner grid: ~20x40
- 4 players on each team, 2-4 players in wide channels
- In possession: complete 4 passes, then play to a channel player — 1 point
- Channel players are available to both teams
- In defense: defend with 3, one player stays in opposite grid
- If defense intercepts, escape to their outlet player — 1 point
- Defending team does not use channel players
- Rotate teams every 4-6 minutes
activities.field_setup: Inner grid ~20x40, outer grid ~30x50 with wide channels on each side
activities.coaching_points:
- Play out quickly: avoid holding the ball and letting opponent close
- Watch for unnecessary dribbling in tight spaces
- Avoid forcing passes into defenders: find better options
- Listen for communication from teammates
- Come wider faster to provide support
activities.flexibility_notes:
- Remove wide channels for a simpler version
- Adjust pass requirement (3 or 5) based on ability level
- Can remove channels and add small end goals for the defending team

activities.title: Passing and Reestablishing Shape
activities.summary: Possession game requiring teams to complete passes then move the entire unit to the next grid, reestablishing attacking shape in transition.
activities.description:
- Two grids, each 16x32 with a line down the center
- Goals on end lines
- 5v3 or 5v2 per grid (4v2 option)
- Possession team: complete 4 passes, then play to one player on the other side of the center line
- Entire team joins on the other side, reestablishing shape
- If turned over, defending team can score on either goal
- Cycle teams every 4-6 minutes
activities.field_setup: Two 16x32 grids with center line, goals on end lines
activities.coaching_points:
- Are we congested? Are we finding space?
- Move to open space, or move to open the space for teammates
- Positional interchanges to avoid stale positioning
- Think ahead: where will you need to be after the transition?
activities.flexibility_notes:
- Adjust required passes (3-5) based on team quality
- Can combine both grids into one larger field if numbers are limited

activities.title: Play Throughs
activities.summary: Possession game with a central box and end zones requiring teams to play through wide players to advance, developing line-breaking and combination play.
activities.description:
- 15x15 center box with 5-yard extended end zones
- 2 wing players stationed in opposite side extended boxes
- Teams of 3 inside
- Must play into wing players and then receive into end zones to score
- Defending team cannot play into end zones but can challenge wing players
- Scoring team stays, or rotate every 3 minutes
- Rotate wing players regularly
activities.field_setup: 15x15 center grid with 5-yard end zones, wing players on sides
activities.coaching_points:
- Avoid players standing in a straight line
- Move to open space, or move to open the space
- Use width to create penetration opportunities
- Triangulate to provide options at different levels
activities.flexibility_notes:
- Add more defenders to increase difficulty
- Add a shooting requirement after entering the end zone to link to finishing

activities.title: Tight Space Quick Release
activities.summary: 3v2 attacking exercise in a compressed space to develop composure, decision making, and quick release under pressure.
activities.description:
- Setup: width of 18-yard box, approximately double the depth
- 2 defenders, 3 attackers, 1 goalkeeper
- Defender at top of box plays ball in to attacker ~5 yards away
- Play is active immediately
- Attack uses numerical advantage to create a shot on goal
- Rotate after each rep
activities.field_setup: ~18 yards wide x ~36 yards deep, large goal on one end
activities.coaching_points:
- Use numerical advantage: find the free player
- Stay composed under pressure
- Play out quickly before defenders recover positions
- Dribble only when clearly better than a pass
activities.flexibility_notes:
- Start with 3v1 to simplify decision making, progress to 3v2
- Can play without a keeper for possession focus

activities.title: 2v1s - Attacking Options
activities.summary: 2v1 attacking drill focusing on off-ball movement and providing options immediately after the first pass.
activities.description:
- 12x8 field with small goals, 2 grids running simultaneously
- Defender plays ball to attackers on goal posts to start
- Attackers must complete a pass before shooting
- Off-ball attacker must provide a clear passing option at all times
- Rotate all positions after each rep
activities.field_setup: 12x8 grids with small goals
activities.coaching_points:
- After passing, the passer must move immediately to create a new option: avoid standing still
- Guided question: how could you create an attacking option after passing?
- Off-ball attacker: provide a diagonal or vertical option, not a flat line
activities.flexibility_notes: - Progress to 3v2 to increase decision-making complexity

activities.title: 3v2s - Attack Forward
activities.summary: 3v2 attacking drill emphasizing triangular spacing and forward-focused attacking options.
activities.description:
- 25x20 field with large goals
- Defenders start on posts and play ball to attackers at opposite edge of field
- Attackers must complete a pass before shooting
- Two off-ball attackers must provide options: avoid flat line alignment
- Rotate all positions after each rep
activities.field_setup: 25x20 field with large goals
activities.coaching_points:
- Avoid all attackers in a flat line: use triangles, spread, and depth
- Guided question: how could you position yourself to create better forward options?
- Look for diagonal and penetrating runs from off-ball players
activities.flexibility_notes:
- Reduce to 2v1 to simplify, or increase to 4v3 for more complexity
- Specify one attacker starts wide to practice wide attacking options

activities.title: 3v2 Toward Goal
activities.summary: 3v2 combining dribbling and passing toward a large goal, emphasizing driving into space and maintaining attacking shape.
activities.description:
- 3 attackers vs 2 defenders toward a full-size goal
- Ball starts centrally with an attacker
- Ball carrier looks to drive forward into space if available
- Off-ball attackers make advancing and supporting runs
- Maintain triangular shape throughout
- Wingers look to cut in on through balls or drop into backward support
activities.field_setup: Half-field width, approximately 50 yards long, full-size goal
activities.coaching_points:
- Drive forward into space if it is there
- Look to make advancing runs off the ball
- Maintain triangular shape
- Wing option: cut in on a through ball or drop into backward support
activities.flexibility_notes:
- Add a third defender for extra pressure
- Specify starting positions to practice formation-specific shapes

activities.title: 2v1 Passing Pattern - Inverted Wings
activities.summary: Combination passing pattern focusing on inverted winger and overlapping full back movement to develop wide attacking interplay.
activities.description:
- Two groups: inverted players and overlap players
- Basic pattern: 2 players one side, 1 in the middle, 1 on opposite side
- Inverted player receives the ball, overlapping player makes run outside
- Play to overlapping player, who plays to next line
- Flip central players every 2 minutes, flip sides every 4 minutes
- Second phase: introduce STR/CAM/WNG runs, crosses, cutbacks, and inverted recovery runs
activities.field_setup: Half-field width, organized in channels
activities.coaching_points:
- Inverted player: get wide before inverting infield
- Direction of first touch determines next action: set up the move
- Overlap player: time the run to avoid being caught offside
- Watch for players not getting wide enough
activities.flexibility_notes:
- Start with just the basic overlapping pattern before adding inverted cuts
- Can extend with a crossing and finishing component at the end

activities.title: Modified 3v2 - Wing and Full Back
activities.summary: Attacking drill with a wide player and overlapping full back against two defenders, developing the wide-to-central combination.
activities.description:
- Setup: GK, 3-4 defenders, 4-5 attackers
- Wing + FB start out wide, STR positions centrally
- Ball starts with full back, slightly inside or behind
- Full back plays into wing player, makes overlapping or underlapping run
- STR gets into the box centrally
- Attack uses combinations to create a shooting opportunity
- Rotate attack and defense after each rep
activities.field_setup: ~50x30 field with large goal
activities.coaching_points:
- Look for shooting opportunities early
- Play the open man: don't force it
- Drive into space when it opens
- STR: get into the box centrally
activities.flexibility_notes: - Constrain to specific combinations (overlap, underlap, cutback) to isolate skills

activities.title: Overlap Attack
activities.summary: Attacking drill focusing on the overlapping run to provide width and additional attacking options off the ball.
activities.description:
- Setup: ~45x25 field, 3 sets of attackers, rotating defenders, balls start centrally
- Ball played left or right, receiving player attacks forward
- Passer makes overlapping run to the outside
- Supporting attacker makes a penetrating or supporting run
- Look to play when appropriate: don't force combinations
- Rotate defenders after each rep, rotate attackers every few reps
activities.field_setup: ~45x25 field, cones marking wing channels
activities.coaching_points:
- First touch: direction of touch changes available options
- Play fast enough so the overlapping run is not blocked
- Adjust movement when ball goes wide: create a penetrating run toward goal
- Guided question: how does your first touch change your options?
activities.flexibility_notes:
- Start with a passive defender and progress to active defense
- Can add a small goal on each end for the defending team to score on

activities.title: 4v2 Finishing
activities.summary: Attacking drill with numerical advantage emphasizing quick combination play and clinical finishing.
activities.description:
- 4 attackers vs 2 defenders attacking a full-size goal
- Ball played out from a defender to one of the attackers to start
- Attackers look to create a piercing through ball or quick combination
- Shoot quick, hard, and low
- Rotate defenders after each rep
activities.field_setup: ~30x20 field with large goal
activities.coaching_points:
- Limit touches: avoid extra touches before shooting
- Look for piercing passes that create immediate shooting opportunities
- Shoot quick: hard and low
- Move to support after passing: don't watch
activities.flexibility_notes:
- Start with 4v1 for simpler decision making
- Add a keeper to make finishing more realistic

activities.title: Control Set Shoot
activities.summary: Finishing circuit focused on receiving, setting up with a touch, and shooting efficiently from the edge of the box.
activities.description:
- 4-cone diamond setup
- Players queue left or right of the diamond
- Partner plays ball to feet
- Player controls, sets (one touch to set up), then shoots
- V1: basic control-set-shoot
- V2: add a hesitation before the set touch
- Progression: add a defender who starts off slightly; passer can overlap to provide an option
- Focus on the setup touch, not just the shot
activities.field_setup: 4-cone diamond ~10x10 yards, large goal
activities.coaching_points:
- The setup is more important than the shot: a good setup enables a good shot
- Open hips to create shooting angle
- Strike with finesse for placement, or drive through for power
- Body shape on receiving: set up toward the goal
activities.flexibility_notes:
- Add a V3 with a double touch before shooting
- Progress to an active defender for realistic pressure

activities.title: 3v2 Overlaps Finishing
activities.summary: Finishing combination featuring an overlapping run, striker run, and wide attacker to develop movement into the box.
activities.description:
- Start mostly centrally
- First player plays to second player, makes overlapping run
- Wide player stays in their channel
- One immediate defender plus one coming in as support
- Everyone cycles through, wingers cycle manually
- Can use existing channel markers from adjacent drill
activities.field_setup: Wide channel plus central area, large goal, ~30x40
activities.coaching_points:
- Overlap: time run to receive in space
- Striker or second attacker: make a run to near or far post
- Wide player: hold width to stretch defense
- Play the open man rather than forcing a shot
activities.flexibility_notes:
- Specify a cutback finish to practice crossing into the box
- Extend with a Trailing Runner Finishing rep after

activities.title: Trailing Runner Finishing
activities.summary: Finishing drill with a winger crossing and attackers stretching the defense while a third player delays to arrive late for a finish.
activities.description:
- 2 defenders, 3 attackers, 1 winger
- Ball played into the winger's space
- Winger takes 2 touches max to cross
- 2 attackers stretch: one near post, one far post
- Third attacker delays their run to arrive at the edge of the box as the ball arrives
- Winger delivers, attackers look to finish
- Rotate all positions
activities.field_setup: Wide channel plus box area, large goal
activities.coaching_points:
- Near-post and far-post runners: time runs to avoid offside
- Third attacker: delay so you arrive as the ball arrives — don't overrun
- Winger: 2-touch maximum, deliver quickly
- All attackers: follow shots
activities.flexibility_notes: - Can specify delivery type: low cutback, high cross, or near-post driven ball

activities.title: Overlap Cutbacks - Crossing
activities.summary: Crossing drill where wide players deliver cutbacks and crosses with central attackers making timed runs to finish.
activities.description:
- Large goal with 18-yard box marked
- ~50x25 field with ~5x25 wide channels on each side
- Balls start at outside edges
- Attacking player plays into wing player in channel
- Wing player (2-3 touches max): cannot shoot, must deliver a cross or cutback
- Defender cuts off passing angles but cannot defend in the channel
- Attacking players time runs to finish
- Play ends if defender intercepts
- Rotate wing and central players regularly
activities.field_setup: 50x25 field plus 5-yard wide channels each side, large goal with 18-yard box marked
activities.coaching_points:
- Wing players: what are you doing with your first touch?
- Wing players: are you playing quickly enough — deliver before defenders close?
- Wing players: set up cross or cutback angle with your second touch
- Attacking players: time runs — arrive as the ball arrives
- Attacking players: finish low and to corners
activities.flexibility_notes:
- Specify delivery type to isolate a skill: cutback only, driven cross, floated cross
- Add a second defender to challenge inside attackers

activities.title: Cutback Finishing
activities.summary: Finishing exercise with a wide attacker driving at the 18-yard box and playing cutbacks for teammates to finish on first touch.
activities.description:
- Wide attacker starts wide and moves backward to create width
- Receives ball and drives toward the 18-yard box
- Plays cutback ball to teammates who delay their runs
- Teammates time runs to arrive as the ball is cut back
- Rotation: far left gets ball first, rotates left to right
- Progression: add a defender
activities.field_setup: Outer half of field, large goal, wide positions marked with cones
activities.coaching_points:
- Wide attacker: drive forward with pace, commit the defender
- Cutback: play the ball when you can still get it across
- Runners: delay the run so you arrive from depth — don't overrun
- First touch finish: set up quickly and shoot low
activities.flexibility_notes: - Can split into 3 teams: 2 playing scrimmage while 1 works on finishing

activities.title: Breakaway Attack
activities.summary: Fast-break attack drill where players start in a nearly flat line and quickly attack the goal after receiving wide.
activities.description:
- Players start in almost a flat line across the field
- Ball played in to a wide player
- Players close ball down quickly
- Either attack the goal directly or find a teammate in a better position
- Defense: goal is only to clear the ball
- Rotate after each rep
activities.field_setup: ~Half field width, players in flat line, large goal
activities.coaching_points:
- Close ball down quickly: speed of transition is the advantage
- Attack the goal if you have space
- Find the teammate in the better position if you don't
- Urgency: make the decision before the defense recovers
activities.flexibility_notes:
- Add a trailing runner for a more realistic counter scenario
- Add a time constraint (3 seconds to shoot) to increase urgency

activities.title: 4+2v3 Aerial Knock Downs
activities.summary: Aerial combination drill where a striker knocks down a long ball for supporting runners to attack quickly.
activities.description:
- 4 outside players + 2 central attackers vs 3 defenders
- Ball played in to either striker
- Striker knocks down or lays off to a wide player or supporting runner
- Attack quickly: play back or wide and attack immediately
- Back defender joins to apply pressure after knockdown
- Optional adjustments:
  - Opt 1: 2 CB + 1 CM vs 2 STR + 2 CAM
  - Opt 2: 1 CB + 1 CM vs 1 STR + 2 CAM
activities.field_setup: ~40x30 field, large goal
activities.coaching_points:
- Striker: knock down to feet or flick wide — don't hold under pressure
- Supporting runners: time arrival for the second ball
- Attack quickly after the knock-down
- Wide players: get into position early to receive
activities.flexibility_notes: - Adjust numbers based on roster using optional configurations above

activities.title: Aerial Control and Passing Lines
activities.summary: Small group aerial control drill developing the ability to control aerial balls under light pressure and play quickly.
activities.description:
- 5-8 players per group in 3 lines
- Player 3 (server): ~10 yards from Player 2 (receiver)
- Player 2: ~5 yards from a cone behind them
- Player 1 applies light pressure on Player 2
- Player 3 throws or chips ball to Player 2
- Player 2 controls the aerial ball under light pressure from Player 1
- Player 3 makes a run outside to receive the next pass
- All players rotate positions
activities.field_setup: 3 lines, ~10 yards between server and receiver, cones marking the pressure zone
activities.coaching_points:
- Eyes up early: track the incoming ball
- Body shape: get in line with the ball's flight path
- Pressure player: challenging enough to be realistic, not so much that you take the ball
- Play out quickly once controlled
activities.flexibility_notes: - Progress to 2v1 Control and Passing - Aerial for active defensive pressure

activities.title: 2v1 Control and Passing - Aerial
activities.summary: Progression of aerial control drill where the controlling player joins the attack after passing, creating a 2v1 to finish.
activities.description:
- Same setup as Aerial Control and Passing Lines
- Player 2 controls aerial ball from the server (Player 3)
- Player 2 plays to Player 3 who has made a supporting run outside
- Player 2 then joins on the attack: 2v1 vs Player 1
- Mini goal on far end
- Rotate all players after each rep
activities.field_setup: ~15 yards total length, mini goal on one end
activities.coaching_points:
- Controlling player: after passing, make a quick run to support the attack
- Server: make your outside run early
- 2v1: use the numerical advantage — don't overcomplicate it
activities.flexibility_notes: - Can constrain to one-touch finish to focus on combination play

activities.title: Crossing and Finishing
activities.summary: Channel crossing drill where wide players deliver balls for central attackers to time runs and finish.
activities.description:
- Two wide channels on sides of the field
- Wide players deliver balls from channels into the box
- Two central attackers time runs and finish
- Vary delivery: floated cross, driven low cross, cutback
- Rotate wide players and central attackers regularly
activities.field_setup: Wide channels on each side, central area ~20x30, large goal
activities.coaching_points:
- Timing of runs: arrive as ball arrives
- Finishing: low and toward corners
- Wide players: deliver within 2 touches
- Check shoulders before making runs to find space
activities.flexibility_notes:
- Add a trailing runner who arrives just after the main attackers
- Add a passive then active defender to progress difficulty

activities.title: Dribbling Competition
activities.summary: Fun competitive dribbling races in small teams to build ball control at speed and confidence on the ball.
activities.description:
- Break into 3-6 teams
- Various dribbling courses or relay races
- Options: cone slaloms, speed dribbles, directional change courses
- Teams race: fastest team wins the round
- Mix teams and courses each round
activities.field_setup: Multiple small courses or lanes, cones for slaloms
activities.coaching_points:
- Keep ball close: don't knock it too far ahead
- Touch the ball with every step at speed
- Use both feet when changing direction
activities.flexibility_notes: - Can require specific skill moves (step over, scissors) as mandatory elements in the course

activities.title: 1v1 Play-Ins - Wish Bone Build Up
activities.summary: Build-up play exercise with a center back receiving aerial balls from wide positions under forward pressure, developing composure in defense.
activities.description:
- Wish Bone formation starting positions:
  - 1-2 players at each wing position
  - 2 players at CB position
  - 1 player at STR position
- Wing player plays ball in the air to CB
- CB traps, looks to play it back to either wing player
- STR challenges CB as soon as they have a touch
- Rotation:
  - Wing player who played it → STR
  - STR → CB
  - CB → wing player who did not play it
  - Wing player who did not play it → other wing position
- Progression: wing players move down lines to receive; STR challenges immediately on contact
activities.field_setup: 15x10 space, Wish Bone formation marked with ~4 cones
activities.coaching_points:
- CB: scan to see where the space is before the ball arrives
- CB: control well enough to give yourself options
- CB: be poised and ready for ball to arrive
- CB: play quickly to avoid being dispossessed under pressure
activities.flexibility_notes: - Progress to full back + CDM build-up to involve more players

activities.title: Play Out of Back
activities.summary: Structured build-up exercise where the defensive unit plays out from the back under active pressing from an attacking team.
activities.description:
- DEF: GK, 3 CB, 2 WB, 2 CDM
- ATK: 2 WNG, 1 STR, 1 CAM, 2 CM
- Ball played in from the side to CBs
- Defense looks to play out and score on 2 mini goals wide
- ATK presses and tries to score on GK upon winning the ball
- Focus on playing quickly to avoid the counter-press
activities.field_setup: Quarter field, large goal for defenders, 2 mini goals wide for defense to attack
activities.coaching_points:
- Secure the ball first: clean first touch
- Look to play forward first; sideways or backward only if forward is closed
- Play quickly to avoid the counter-press
- WB and CDM: provide clear support angles wide and centrally
activities.flexibility_notes: - Start with a passive pressing team before making the press active

activities.title: Staggered Defense 2v2s
activities.summary: 2v2 defending drill with staggered starting positions, developing first-defender pressure and second-defender delay.
activities.description:
- 10x15 field with small goals
- Two separate starting zones for defenders
- No pass needed to advance
- 3-minute sets, flip field after 2nd set
- Switch player lines in group between reps
- Baseline defender plays ball in to attacking team
- Sideline defender closes to prevent quick break
- Defense: first defender pressures, second delays and covers
activities.field_setup: 10x15 field with small goals, two color-coded starting zones
activities.coaching_points:
- When ball is played: can we force the overload on the receiver?
- First defender: eliminate passing option, force to the sideline
- What happens if we close too slowly?
- How do we know which way to push the opponent?
activities.flexibility_notes: - Extend to 3v3 for more complex defensive shape work

activities.title: Delaying in Midfield
activities.summary: Defending exercise on a larger field where the defensive team practices delaying a counter-attack while shape is reestablished.
activities.description:
- 60x40 field with small goals on each end
- Optional: keepers playing as field players
- No passing requirement
- After a turnover, defense immediately looks to delay the counter
- Defending team drops off and blocks direct paths to goal
- Get narrow, protect the lane, force wide or backward
- Engagement is patient: allow teammates time to recover positions
activities.field_setup: 60x40 field with small goals on each end
activities.coaching_points:
- How can we prevent the quick break on a turnover?
- Drop off and block the direct path to goal
- Force wide or backwards: don't dive in
- Patience: delay long enough to let teammates recover
activities.flexibility_notes: - Can designate one team to always defend to focus exclusively on their behavior

activities.title: 2v2 Defensive Shape
activities.summary: 2v2 defending drill emphasizing communication, body shape, and switching defensive roles as the ball moves.
activities.description:
- 10-15x15 field with small goals
- 1 attacker and 1 defender on opposite goal posts; 1 attacker and 1 defender on side lines
- Goal-line attacker plays ball to teammate to start
- Defenders enter: one presses ball carrier, other builds cover and balance shape
- Variation 1 (recover): defenders press and delay, looking to regain shape
- Variation 2 (create shape): defenders focus on compactness and switching marks as ball moves
activities.field_setup: 10-15x15 field with small goals, 4 starting positions marked
activities.coaching_points:
- Communication is critical: especially when the second pass switches who presses and who supports
- Body shape on delay: which way are we pushing them? Where is support?
- Switch marks effectively when the ball moves
- Scan to know where the third attacker is at all times
activities.flexibility_notes:
- Add a third attacker (2v3) to make defending harder
- Allow no pass before shooting for more direct defensive pressure

activities.title: 5v4 Recovery
activities.summary: Defending exercise where a flat back four and CDM must recover and rebuild shape after an attacking line is broken.
activities.description:
- 30x50 field with full goal
- DEF: flat back 4 + CDM starting at ~22 yards
- ATK: 2 wingers, CF, CAM (CAM at ~30 yards, others aligned with D line)
- Ball played from CAM through to a winger, breaking past the fullback and defensive line
- Defense recovers to win ball back
- Attack looks to score
- Rotate positions between reps
activities.field_setup: 30x50 field with large goal, markers at 22-yard and 30-yard lines
activities.coaching_points:
- Communication: who is pressing the ball, who is supporting?
- When lines are broken: who chases, who pressures, who recovers?
- Shape rebuild: where are we trying to force the opponent?
- CDM: read when to drop into the CB position
activities.flexibility_notes: - Run as attack-only first (no recovery attempt) to practice the attacking combination before adding recovery

activities.title: 2v3 Creating Defending Shape
activities.summary: 2 defenders vs 3 attackers to practice creating optimal defending shape with numerical disadvantage.
activities.description:
- 15x25 field with large goal one end, 1 small goal opposite
- 2 defenders at goal posts, 2 attackers on opposite side lines, 1 attacker on back goal with balls
- Attacker plays either wing player; wing player gets 1 more pass before shooting
- Defenders enter: pressure attackers and create shape
- Defenders score 1 point for playing ball out to next sideline players, 2 points for scoring on central goal
- Rotate all positions
activities.field_setup: 15x25 field with large goal one end and small goal opposite
activities.coaching_points:
- Do we switch off marks effectively as the ball moves?
- Are we scanning properly to know where the third attacker is?
- Are we stepping out of position at the right times, or should we be directing teammates?
- As the field shifts, communicate which attackers to pick up
activities.flexibility_notes: - Add a third defender (3v3) to reduce difficulty and emphasize shape

activities.title: Positional Walkthrough - Defensive
activities.summary: Coached walkthrough of defensive positional responsibilities and movement patterns, followed by a live scrimmage.
activities.description:
- Get players into full defensive positions on a half-field setup
- Coach walks through key movements:
  - CDM/CM rotating to cover CB and CDM positions respectively
  - Wide CB pressing to delay forward advancement
  - CB shifting to provide support
  - Directing someone to pick up the striker
- Ball played in by attack, defense responds
- Coach pauses to correct positioning and communication
- Progress to a live scrimmage once understanding is established
activities.field_setup: Half field, ~40x30, large goal or 2-3 small goals
activities.coaching_points:
- As the field shifts, are we communicating which attackers to pick up?
- Are we stepping out of position at the correct times?
- How are we directing teammates who don't see the full picture?
activities.flexibility_notes: - Adjust positional responsibilities to match current team formation

activities.title: Rotation Walk-Through
activities.summary: Coached half-field walkthrough of defensive rotation assignments focusing on wing back, CDM, and CB adjustments.
activities.description:
- Half-field setup
- ATK: 2-1-3 (6 players)
- DEF: 3-4-1-2 (8 players) + GK
- Wing backs start further up field
- Rotation 1: far-side wing back rotates into FB, attack swings ball through midfielders, defense shifts
- Rotation 2: dropped CDM drops into CB, pushed CDM tucks in on CAM
- Coach walks through each rotation, pausing to show movement
- Progress to Defend and Escape
activities.field_setup: Half field, ~50x40
activities.coaching_points:
- Far-side wing back: rotate to FB when ball switches sides
- CDM: recognize when to drop into CB and when to tuck in
- Communication is critical: defense must shift as a unit
activities.flexibility_notes: - Adjust rotation rules to match current formation

activities.title: Defend and Escape
activities.summary: Defending exercise where the defensive team must win the ball back and play out to outside goals, combining defensive shape with transition.
activities.description:
- Same setup as Rotation Walk-Through
- Add 2 small outside goals for the defending team to score on after winning the ball
- Ball played in by attack, must switch play to start
- Defense shifts to cover the switch
- Win the ball back and escape quickly to outside goals
- Rotate positions regularly
activities.field_setup: Half field, ~50x40, large goal one end, 2 small goals on sides
activities.coaching_points:
- How do we shift as a unit when the ball is switched?
- After winning the ball: look to escape quickly before attack recovers
- Communication: announce the switch before it happens
activities.flexibility_notes: - Constrain the attack to specific movements to isolate defensive rotations

activities.title: Recovery Progression
activities.summary: Staged defending exercise where a defensive unit recovers and applies pressure after a ball is played in.
activities.description:
- Stage 1: simplified recovery shape with light pressure
- Stage 2:
  - Full goal, ~50x25 field
  - Ball starts on one side of the attack
  - Attacker plays ball in to a teammate
  - Defense activates and recovers once ball is played in
  - Attack must complete 2 passes before shooting
  - Defense works to cut off options and drop into proper positions
- Rotate after each rep
activities.field_setup: ~50x25 field, large goal
activities.coaching_points:
- How can we cut off their options?
- Are we chasing the ball or finding proper spots to drop into?
- First defender: apply immediate pressure on the ball
- Supporting defenders: find passing lane angles to cover
activities.flexibility_notes:
- Omit Stage 1 if the group is experienced
- Increase attack's pass requirement (3 or 4) if defense is finding it easy

activities.title: Field Pressing
activities.summary: Team defending exercise where the attacking unit presses the defending team immediately after a ball is played in, simulating a high press.
activities.description:
- DEF: GK, 3 CB, 2 WB, 1 MID
- ATK: 2 FWD, 2 WB, 3 MID
- ~50x30 field
- 2 mini goals for the defending team to score on
- Coach plays ball in to DEF, ATK presses immediately
- Defense looks to play out and score on mini goals
- ATK wins ball: play to a mini goal or back to coach for reset
activities.field_setup: ~50x30 field, large goal for defenders, 2 mini goals for attackers
activities.coaching_points:
- Are we moving as a unit: coordinated press, not individual chasing?
- Are we communicating: who triggers the press?
- Are we over-committing: leaving space in behind?
- What are we doing once we win the ball back?
activities.flexibility_notes:
- Can specify the trigger for the press (GK distribution, back-pass)
- Adjust field size: smaller = more pressure, larger = more recovery

activities.title: 2v2 Pressured Defense
activities.summary: 1v1 building to 2v2 exercise focused on tight marking, preventing the attacker from turning, and switching when a pass is played.
activities.description:
- Two goals, field 10x15
- Defender sets on attacker's back before play starts
- Teammate plays ball into attacker
- Defender's only job: prevent the attacker from turning
- Attacker can play in their teammate, but teammate cannot advance past 1/4 of the field until the ball is played in
- Additional defender enters once pass is played
- Play continues as 2v2
activities.field_setup: 10x15 field with two small goals
activities.coaching_points:
- Mark intelligently: tight enough to prevent turning, balanced enough to react to passes
- Body shape: goal-side of attacker, showing them backward
- Communicate with teammate: who steps, who covers
- Stay with your mark when the ball is played: don't chase the ball
activities.flexibility_notes: - Start 1v1 only (no teammate) to isolate individual defending technique

activities.title: 3v3 Pressured Defense Switch
activities.summary: Progression of 2v2 Pressured Defense with additional attackers to create switching and communication demands.
activities.description:
- Same as 2v2 Pressured Defense but field expands to 15x25
- Add 2 new attacking players in a top-left area
- Defense must communicate and switch marks when the ball is passed to the extra players
- Additional defenders engage when ball goes wide
- Rotate teams regularly
activities.field_setup: 15x25 field
activities.coaching_points:
- Communication: call switches early — don't wait until you're beat
- Mark intelligently: don't follow a player blindly out of position
- Are we identifying the correct marks?
- Collective pressure: act as a unit when extra attackers join
activities.flexibility_notes: - Increase to 4v4 if numbers allow for more realistic conditions

activities.title: Switch Field Attack - Defensive Rotations
activities.summary: Positional exercise where the defense tracks an attack switching the ball across the field, then engages once ball reaches the weak side.
activities.description:
- DEF: GK, 3 CB, 2 WB, 2 CDM (7 players)
- ATK: 2 WNG, 1 STR, 1 CAM, 2 CM (6 players)
- Large goal one side, small goals in opposite corners
- Attack starts from one side and shifts ball to the other side
- Defense follows and shifts but does not engage until ball reaches opposite winger
- Once ball reaches opposite winger: attack is free, defense engages
- Defense scores on small goals when they win the ball
activities.field_setup: Half field, large goal one side, 2 small goals in opposite corners
activities.coaching_points:
- Wing back: rotate into FB when play shifts away from your side
- Far-side WB: drop into CDM position
- CDM: shift to cover the space vacated by WB
- Communicate the shift: everyone moves together
activities.flexibility_notes: - Add a constraint that attack must play at least 3 passes before switching to force more defensive movement

activities.title: Over the River Switch Play
activities.summary: Possession game variant where teams must play through both channels before switching, emphasizing switching the point of attack.
activities.description:
- Same field setup as Across the River - Wide Channels
- Small goals on ends
- Teams of 4, channel players available to both teams
- 3 defenders at a time
- Must play into both channels before switching play to score
- If defense intercepts, can shoot on small goals immediately
- Rotate teams regularly
activities.field_setup: Inner grid ~20x40, outer grid ~30x50 with wide channels, small goals on ends
activities.coaching_points:
- Play out quickly: don't allow opponent to close
- Are we using width to create the switch?
- Avoid unnecessary dribbling in tight space
- Find better options rather than forcing into defenders
- Come wider faster to support possession
activities.flexibility_notes: - Allow scoring after one channel (instead of both) for a simpler version

activities.title: Free Kicks
activities.summary: Set piece practice focusing on direct free kicks and indirect layoff combinations from various positions.
activities.description:
- Mark 18-yard box from goal
- Standard wall setup (wall on near post side)
- Variations to practice:
  - Layoff and drive low: taker lays off to teammate who drives
  - Fake kick: taker dummies over ball, second player plays wide
  - Direct kick: driven low to far post
- Rotate takers and receivers
- Progress from unopposed to full defending team with wall
activities.field_setup: Various positions outside 18-yard box, full goal with wall and keeper
activities.coaching_points:
- Identify opportunities: direct shot vs. combination play vs. switch
- Be creative, but keep it simple and rehearsed
- Wall: protect the near post angle
- Non-shooting players: make realistic runs to occupy defenders
activities.flexibility_notes: - Practice from wide positions for crossing free kicks

activities.title: Corner Kicks - Defensive
activities.summary: Defensive corner kick organization and execution practice focusing on marking, positioning, and clearances.
activities.description:
- Position all defenders:
  - Near-sided FB on near post
  - CBs on 6-yard box
  - Keeper 2/3 back in goal
  - Remaining players man-mark every attacker (tight, goal-side)
- Communication calls: 'Away', 'Outside', 'Step', 'Press/Pressure', 'I got man'
- Marking technique: get narrow, CBs remain central, get physical but avoid fouls
- Pressing: track the man, don't chase the ball
- Clearance: outside and out; heading technique — up and out
activities.field_setup: Full goal with 18-yard box, attacking team takes corners
activities.coaching_points:
- Are we close enough on marks before ball is delivered?
- How do we move with our mark as they try to evade?
- Outside first for clearances: avoid clearing back into the box
- Every player should have a mark before the corner is taken
activities.flexibility_notes: - Run simultaneously with Corner Kicks - Offensive: one team attacks, other defends

activities.title: Corner Kicks - Offensive
activities.summary: Attacking corner kick practice focusing on delivery, run timing, and finishing.
activities.description:
- Attacking setup:
  - One player in front of keeper
  - One player on 6-yard box
  - Remaining players at top of box
  - No short corners
  - Ball over the 6-yard box: in-swinger preferred
  - Option: direct shot from corner
- Run timing: avoid overrunning
- Try to evade marking with movement before delivery
- Finishing: heading technique, aim low, follow shots
activities.field_setup: Full goal with 18-yard box, defending team in position
activities.coaching_points:
- Cross placement: ball needs to clear the 6-yard box and be attackable
- Run timing: arrive as the ball arrives — don't overrun
- Heading: attack the ball with purpose, strike with forehead, aim low
- Follow shots: always be in position to follow up
activities.flexibility_notes: - Run simultaneously with Corner Kicks - Defensive

activities.title: Penalty Kicks
activities.summary: Penalty kick practice for all players to develop composure, technique, and a reliable placement.
activities.description:
- All players rotate through taking penalties
- GK practices positioning and reads
- Each player takes 2-3 kicks per round
- Encourage players to identify their preferred placement (low corner)
- Keepers must guess direction and commit: reward decisiveness
- Debrief: placement over power, decide before approach, controlled run-up
activities.field_setup: Full goal with penalty spot
activities.coaching_points:
- Decide on placement before starting run-up: don't change your mind
- Placement over power: low and to the corner
- GK: read body shape during run-up, commit to a side
- Stay calm: control breathing before the kick
activities.flexibility_notes: - Add competitive pressure (score or go out) to simulate a game scenario

activities.title: Scrimmage
activities.summary: Free small-sided or full game to apply session concepts in a competitive context.
activities.description:
- Standard setup: two goals, teams of equal size
- Small-sided options: 5v5, 6v6, 7v7, 9v9
- Common field sizes: 30x50, 40x60, or full field
- Rotation options: 5-minute cycles with substitutes, winning team stays on
- GK or field players in goal depending on session focus
- Coach observes and applies session coaching points
- Debrief as needed: pause to address patterns but allow free play
activities.field_setup: Variable: 30x50 to full field, two goals
activities.coaching_points:
- Apply session coaching points in a game context
- Use guided questions rather than direct instruction
- Allow players time to solve problems before intervening
activities.flexibility_notes:
- Use small goals to encourage possession play
- Specify a formation to practice tactical shape
- Use 3-team format: 2 play while 1 observes or works on fitness
